summary: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity mid-circuit erasure detection in transmon dual-rail qubits using a symmetrically coupled readout resonator (SRO), achieving 384 ns erasure checks with $6.0(2) \times 10^{-4}$ residual error per check and enabling continuous parallel erasure detection during gates at $7.2 \times 10^{-5}$ error per X90 gate. The symmetric coupling achieves $\chi$-matching with $|\chi_{\mathrm{DR}}/\chi| < 1 \times 10^{-2}$ over 600 MHz, suppressing measurement-induced dephasing while maintaining strong erasure-state discrimination.
motivation: Erasure qubits offer higher error thresholds and favorable scaling for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but realizing their advantages requires frequent, fast, high-fidelity mid-circuit erasure checks that minimally disturb the logical subspace—a challenge for previous superconducting implementations with significant overhead or long detection times.
method: A single readout resonator is dispersively and symmetrically coupled to both transmons in a dual-rail pair, with engineered symmetric couplings ($g_{\mathrm{RT1}} = g_{\mathrm{RT2}}$) achieving a zero-crossing of $\chi_{\mathrm{DR}}$ near 4.5 GHz where the logical states experience matched dispersive shifts. Single-shot readout uses 384 ns probes optimized for signal-to-noise ratio while minimizing measurement-induced state transitions; continuous parallel detection exploits $\chi$-matching to monitor erasure events during gate execution.
result: Single-shot erasure detection achieves $2.54(1) \times 10^{-2}$ erasure error and $6.0(2) \times 10^{-4}$ residual error per 384 ns check with $8(3) \times 10^{-5}$ induced dephasing; continuous parallel erasure detection during single-qubit gates yields $7.2 \times 10^{-5}$ X90 error with $< 1 \times 10^{-5}$ detection overhead, demonstrating erasure detection overhead reduction and temporal resolution beneficial for soft-information quantum error correction.
